newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek depos firm, bonds ease, ecu/drachma up.
newsitem.headline: Greek depos firm, bonds ease, ecu/drachma up.

text.p: Greece's depos were trading 20 to 30 basis points higher with the rise more accentuated in short-tenors, and forex forwards were little changed, dealers said.
Bonds opened down and the drachma was weaker against the ecu, breaching the 310 weak resistance.
"Depos have firmed 20 to 30 basis points in periods up to two-months and 10 to 20 basis points in longer periods," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "It is a purely liquidity-driven pick-up."
The liquidity squeeze is linked to the banks' arbitrage play against the central bank, dealers said.

"Banks lend 14-day funds to the central bank at 11.90 percent to come out subsequently and borrow them at much lower rates in one-, two- or one-month periods in the interbank market," the dealer said.

The Bank of Greece drained 100 billion drachmas of 14-day funds at 11.90 percent in its regular fixed rate tender on Wednesday. A 14-day pact of 100 billion drachmas expired so that net liquidity was left intact.
Seven-and 10-year bonds were easier, having shed 10 basis points in terms of price, bond dealers said.
"Seven-and 10-year bonds opened softer," said a bond trader. "It is the follow-up effect from yesterday's late selling pressure."
The mark was quoted at 157.46/51 from Wednesday's 157.640 fix, the dollar at 276.15/25 drachmas from 275.070 and the ecu at 309.94/04 from 309.66 drachmas.

"The drachma opened at 309.80/85 against the ecu but ecu/drachma has breached the 310 level, trading currently around 310.05/10," a senior dealer at a private bank said. "I think we will see ecu/drachma at higher levels later on."
Local banks were buying ecus for drachmas in early dealings and the market was quiet, traders said.
